Amazon EC2 accelerated computing and Amazon SageMaker AI

capability 4.3 · readiness 3.1
  1. 20 Nov 2026 · permanent record
    First scored: capability 4.3, readiness 3.1
    The reasoning behind each of the seven scores
    • Capability and differentiation: 4.3
      Anchor 4: all six listed capabilities are shown in AWS documentation and service pages: on-demand and reserved accelerators, managed inference, dedicated capacity, regional availability, security attestations and open-weight model serving. Dedicated tenancy for accelerated instance types specifically was not confirmed. Anchor 5 needs confirmation by a source other than the vendor of the product's capability, which was not found. How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Pricing

Pricing is usually not public. This states what is known, what is estimated, and what is not public.

Pricing
KnownOn-demand inference is charged per token. Examples on the pricing page: Mistral Large 3 in US East at US$0.50 per million input tokens and US$1.50 per million output tokens; OpenAI gpt-oss-120b in Sydney at US$0.1545 and US$0.6180.; Batch inference is about 50% below on-demand for select models. Service tiers: Flex at a 50% discount to Standard, Priority at a 75% premium, plus Reserved.; Provisioned Throughput is charged per model unit per hour with no commitment or 1-month and 6-month commitments, for example Cohere Command at US$49.50, US$39.60 and US$23.77.; Guardrails content filters US$0.15 per 1,000 text units; Knowledge Bases US$5.00 per GB per month of index storage and US$1.00 per 1,000 Retrieve calls; Intelligent Prompt Routing US$1 per 1,000 requests.; Global cross-Region inference is priced about 10% below geographic routing. Questions to ask the vendor (3)

  1. Who are the largest shareholders of Amazon.com, Inc. and does any hold a controlling interest?
    Large shareholders can influence a critical provider's strategy.
  2. Have any large regulated customers moved generative-AI workloads off Amazon Bedrock in the last two years, and why?
    Departures of large customers can signal service or commercial problems.
  3. Have there been any leadership departures, investigations or governance issues at AWS in the last two years that a customer should know about?
    Leadership instability or misconduct can affect a provider's direction and reputation.

  2. 2026-07-23 · vulnerability disclosure Amazon Web Services
    AWS discloses CVE-2026-16796 in the Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK

    AWS disclosed in security bulletin 2026-065-AWS on 2026-07-23 that a second flaw in the install_packages() method of the bedrock-agentcore Python SDK, in versions before 1.18.1, could let a remote authenticated user run arbitrary commands in the Code Interpreter sandbox through crafted package-name arguments. AWS credited an individual researcher and BeyondTrust Phantom Labs and said version 1.18.1 fixes it. The bulletin does not state whether exploitation is known. Amazon Web Services (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-06-17 · vulnerability disclosure Amazon Web Services
    AWS discloses CVE-2026-12530 in the Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK

    AWS disclosed in security bulletin 2026-044-AWS on 2026-06-17 that the install_packages() method of the Code Interpreter client in the bedrock-agentcore Python SDK, versions 1.1.3 up to but not including 1.6.1, sanitised package names with an incomplete blocklist, so crafted arguments could redirect package resolution to a third-party server or expose sandbox files. AWS said version 1.6.1 fixes it. The bulletin does not state whether exploitation is known. Amazon Web Services (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

    Third Circuit affirms dismissal of Illinois biometric privacy claims against Pindrop

    According to the precedential opinion filed by the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit on 2026-05-12 in McGoveran v. Amazon Web Services, Inc. and Pindrop Security, Inc. (No. 24-3215), Illinois callers alleged that Amazon and Pindrop collected their voiceprints without consent, in breach of the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, when authenticating calls to John Hancock. The court affirmed the district court, including its dismissal of the claims against Pindrop under the Act's exemption for financial institutions subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. The press accounts rest on one original report with unnamed sources; Amazon's statement does not say whether Kiro was in use.   13. 2025-10-19 · outage Amazon Web Services
    AWS US-EAST-1 disruption traced to a DynamoDB DNS automation fault

    AWS stated in its post-event summary that a service disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region ran from 11:48 PM PDT on 19 October 2025 to 2:20 PM PDT on 20 October 2025. AWS attributed it to a latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management that left the regional endpoint with an empty DNS record, with knock-on effects on EC2 instance launches, Network Load Balancer, Lambda, ECS, EKS, Fargate, Amazon Connect, STS, console sign-in and Redshift. Amazon Bedrock is not named among the affected services. AWS said it disabled the DNS automation worldwide pending a fix and would add safeguards.
